points.t: A patient on (or recently off) **pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab** or **dabrafenib + trametinib** with **any new symptom**.
Checkpoint inhibitors **release T-cell brakes**, so autoimmune inflammation can hit any organ, even months after stopping.
Ask **‘are you on cancer treatment?’**; contact the **24-hour acute oncology hotline** rather than treating alone; check interactions.
**Colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, myocarditis, hypophysitis / adrenal crisis, new type 1 diabetes / DKA, SJS / TEN.**

cause.lead: Taking the brakes off the immune system.
points: Anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab, nivolumab), anti-CTLA-4 (ipilimumab), anti-LAG-3 (relatlimab) unleash T cells against melanoma.
The same T cells can attack normal organs: **immune-related adverse events (irAEs)**.
Onset **weeks to months after the first dose, even after stopping**; ipi + nivo: grade 3–4 irAEs in > half.
BRAF / MEK inhibitors cause a different, drug-specific set.

visuals.caption: Checkpoint inhibitor antibodies block the brake on T cells so they can attack melanoma; the same release can inflame normal organs.
visuals.alt: T cell, blocking antibody and melanoma cell

points: **Gut (colitis)**: diarrhoea ≥ 4 above baseline, blood, pain → **same-day acute oncology**; don’t just give loperamide.
**Liver**: raised ALT / AST, jaundice. **Lung**: new cough, breathlessness, hypoxia; don’t assume infection.
**Endocrine**: hypophysitis (headache, fatigue, low sodium), thyroiditis, adrenal insufficiency, **new type 1 diabetes / DKA**: often permanent.
**Skin**: rash, itch, **vitiligo** (linked with response), lichenoid, bullous pemphigoid; rarely SJS / TEN.
Kidney (nephritis); **heart (myocarditis)**, myasthenia, myositis: emergency; joints (arthritis).
**BRAF / MEK**: **pyrexia** (dabrafenib + trametinib), photosensitivity (vemurafenib), new SCC / KA / naevi, QT, LVEF fall, serous retinopathy, hand–foot reaction.

visuals.caption: Immune-related adverse events can affect almost any organ: pituitary, thyroid, lungs, heart, liver, adrenals, bowel and skin.

points: **“Are you on cancer treatment?”**; alert card + **24-hour hotline** (UKONS triage).
TFTs, glucose, cortisol, sodium, LFT, U&E as directed.
Infection (e.g. *C. difficile*), other drug reactions, progression.

cards.name: Infection
cards.clue: *C. difficile*, chest infection: but don’t assume.

points: **Never start immunosuppression independently**: acute oncology grades and prescribes (ESMO / UKONS).
Skin grade 1–2: emollient + topical steroid; urgent if blistering / mucosal.
High-dose steroids: **PPI**, **glucose monitoring**, bone protection if prolonged, **PJP prophylaxis (co-trimoxazole)** if ≥ 20 mg prednisolone ≥ 4 weeks, **steroid emergency card**, sick-day rules.
**Fever** on dabrafenib + trametinib: interrupt per protocol and call oncology.
**Dabrafenib induces CYP3A4**: hormonal contraception unreliable (non-hormonal method); warfarin and others: interaction checker.
Vemurafenib: sun protection; QT-interacting drugs.
Inactivated vaccines fine; live vaccines: specialist advice.
Effective contraception during and for months after (e.g. 4 months after pembrolizumab).

items.t: Chest pain / suspected myocarditis, DKA, adrenal crisis, SJS / TEN.
**Diarrhoea, breathlessness, severe headache, chest pain, new thirst / polyuria** on immunotherapy: acute oncology.
Fever on dabrafenib + trametinib: protocol + oncology team.

pearls.t: “Ring the **hotline**, not the GP’s routine line.” Side-effects are usually treatable if caught early.
Vitiligo on anti-PD-1 often means a better response: sun-protect the white skin.
irAEs can start months after the last dose.

quiz.a: Same-day acute oncology contact; don’t just give loperamide.
CYP3A4 induction lowers hormonal levels: non-hormonal method.
Interrupt per protocol and contact oncology.
